sections.html:
Cheshire is a New Haven County town in the Naugatuck Valley planning region, 14 miles north of New Haven and 25 miles south of Hartford. Waterbury is adjacent, and the town also borders Southington, Meriden, Wallingford, Hamden, Bethany, Prospect and Wolcott.

It covers 33.4 square miles, nearly all of it land, at an elevation of about 230 feet. The 2020 census counted 28,733 residents in 10,169 households, and 10,401 housing units. Cheshire is also the place where the state's center of population sits, according to Census Bureau records.

Town sections include Cheshire Village, a census-designated place with 6,499 residents in 2020. The median household income in 2019 was $120,546, and the town runs on a council-manager form of government headed by a town manager. Cities such as New Haven, Hartford, Waterbury and Meriden are all within a short drive, so commute times come up in showings.

sections.h2: How did Cheshire become a town?
sections.html:
Cheshire was first settled in 1694 as New Cheshire Parish, part of Wallingford. After repeated efforts to gain independence, the parish was allowed to secede and was incorporated as the town of Cheshire in May 1780. The name comes from Cheshire, England.

The area that is now Prospect was part of Cheshire until 1829, known then as Columbia Parish. Cheshire Academy, originally the Episcopal Academy of Connecticut, was founded in the town in 1794.

The population stayed under about 4,400 until 1940, then reached 6,295 in 1950 and 13,383 in 1960, a rise of 112.6 percent in one decade. A jump that size points to heavy mid-century building, so ask an inspector how old your roof, wiring and heating system are.

sections.h2: What is the Cheshire economy like?
sections.html:
Cheshire's largest employers include a food distributor, the state prison system, the town government and several aerospace and logistics firms. The town's 2024 annual financial report lists the following.

Two state prison facilities, Cheshire Correctional Institution (opened in 1913) and Manson Youth Institution (opened in 1982), sit in the northern part of town. Cheshire's nickname is the Bedding Plant Capital of Connecticut.

sections.h2: How do people get around Cheshire?
sections.html:
Most travel in Cheshire is by car. Interstate 691 skirts the northern edge of town, and Interstate 84 passes through the northwest corner.

  • Route 10: the main north-south road and the busiest, with many stoplights.
  • Routes 68 and 70: east-west through Main Street and West Main Street.
  • Route 42: a second east-west road.
  • CTtransit 229: bus service between Waterbury and New Haven along Routes 70 and 10.
  • Commuter express bus: from a lot near Interstate 84 to Hartford.

Traffic is heaviest on Route 10 between Routes 68/70 and Route 42 on weekday mornings and evenings and when the high school lets out around 2 p.m. If your street is on or near Route 10, a buyer will notice the traffic, so be ready to describe the noise level honestly.

Cheshire has one public high school, Cheshire High School, and one public middle school, Dodd Middle School. The four public elementary schools are Chapman, Doolittle, Highland and Barnum. Norton and Chapman were closed and rebuilt, and the Darcy building remains closed.

Private options include Cheshire Academy, founded in 1794 and serving grades 9 to 12 and a post-graduate year, and St. Bridget's, a Catholic school for preschool through eighth grade.

sections.h2: What outdoor attractions affect a Cheshire house?
sections.html:
Cheshire's parks and trails add to the town's appeal. The Farmington Canal Heritage Trail runs through town on its route from Suffield to New Haven, and Roaring Brook Falls, in the southwest corner, is Connecticut's tallest single-drop waterfall and is owned by the Cheshire Land Trust. Town recreation includes Cheshire Park at 75 acres, Bartlem Recreational Area, Mixville Recreation Area and the Cheshire Community Pool, which was renovated in 2016 for year-round indoor swimming.

The National Register lists the Cheshire Historic District around Main Street and the Marion Historic District. The Farmington Canal Lock at 487 North Brooksvale Road and the First Congregational Church are also listed. Ask the town whether your address falls in a historic district before you plan exterior changes.

sections.h2: What does Cheshire's weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Cheshire is inland and receives about 54.6 inches of precipitation a year. January highs average 35 degrees and lows average 15, while July highs average 83, so heating, insulation and roof condition all matter.

Inspectors in a four-season climate look at the roof, gutters, basement moisture, the heating system and any exterior wood. If you have service records for the boiler or furnace and the roof, collect them.

sections.h2: What do Cheshire sellers pay at closing?
sections.html:
Connecticut puts a conveyance tax on deeds for $2,000 or more. The state share is three-quarters of one percent for most homes, with 1.25 percent on the portion of a residential estate above $800,000 up to $2.5 million, and 2.25 percent above that. The town share is one-fourth of one percent.

  • The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded.
  • Cheshire's town code on the form is 025.
  • Exemptions exist, such as transfers between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.

Get a payoff figure for any unpaid bill so it can come out of the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Does a crumbling foundation change the Cheshire sale?
sections.html:
It can change the tax paperwork. The Department of Revenue Services lists an exempt conveyance for a principal residence with a deteriorated concrete foundation caused by pyrrhotite, as determined by a professional engineer. The exemption applies only to the first transfer after the engineer's written evaluation, and the evaluation must be attached to the return. It is not available to an owner receiving financial assistance from the Crumbling Foundations Assistance Fund.

If you suspect a foundation problem, get the evaluation before you decide how to sell, since it affects both the price and the closing documents.

sections.h2: Selling a Cheshire house: when a direct sale fits
sections.html:
A direct cash sale fits an owner who needs speed, an inherited house with updates still pending, or a landlord who wants out. It fits less well when a house is fully updated and likely to draw several retail offers.

Compare what each path nets after commission, repairs, carrying costs and time. We will give you our view of your house and tell you when listing makes more sense.

faqs.q: Where is the center of population of Connecticut?
faqs.a: The center of population of Connecticut is in Cheshire, according to Census Bureau records. It reflects where residents are spread across the state, and it has no effect on your property tax.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance tax in Cheshire?
faqs.a: For most homes the state charges three-quarters of one percent of the price and the town adds one-fourth of one percent. Higher state rates apply to residential estates above $800,000 and to nonresidential property.
Cheshire High School, Dodd Middle School and four elementary schools named Chapman, Doolittle, Highland and Barnum. Check the town's school office to confirm which school serves your street.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cheshire house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A direct buyer can purchase a house in its current condition and price the repairs into the offer. Listing a house that needs work may mean negotiating repair credits after an inspection.

faqs.q: Who sets property taxes in Cheshire?
faqs.a: The Cheshire Assessor sets assessed values and the Tax Collector issues and collects bills. Call both offices for current rates, due dates and a payoff figure.
